title: [HT-002] Re-review of the kill-session wait
description: Narrow re-review of ht-tvn.3 only.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text:
REVIEW PASSED: ht-tvn.3 (commit 9f243d8), the log off now waits for the broker's kill-session answer before it reloads. 0 critical, 0 major, 2 minor, 1 nitpick.

Checked against the brief:
- The wait is armed before the OK click. _confirm_logoff_dialog opens page.expect_response(...) and then clicks inside the with block. In the installed Playwright, EventContextManager.__exit__ cancels the wait when the body raises, so a failed click surfaces as the click's own error.
- The bound has a name and a reason. HorizonTimeouts.kill_session_answer_ms=30_000 carries a comment saying why it exists (the credential-cleanup reload) and that the live answer time is not measured. The SPEC row, the SPEC "Confirming a log off" section, the constructor line, the constants list and the infrastructure README all say this. sync-check is ok.
- An unanswered kill-session still fails closed. On PlaywrightTimeoutError after the click, the adapter logs a warning and the fresh-list poll decides. test_a_log_off_whose_kill_session_is_never_answered_is_not_confirmed covers this: LOGOFF_NOT_CONFIRMED, a screenshot, and the session still DISCONNECTED.
- I checked the predicate against the bundle app-htmlaccess.4eb7424a56fc03317f06.js:
  - Kw.setRequestXML builds session-id, and Oi.createXML wraps it as <broker ...><kill-session>...</kill-session></broker>. So KILL_SESSION_TAG matches, including when the router batches handlers into one document.
  - jscdkPost and postMessage send it as an in-page XHR to .../broker/xml. The mid query, the _ab timestamp and the F5 suffix leave the path containing /broker/xml. The audio, video and unauth Workers do not carry broker traffic, so page.expect_response sees the request.
  - enableCredentialCleanupForHTMLAccess and waitForCredentialClean (3e3) are as the SPEC says.

Measurements (Chromium via PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH=/opt/pw-browsers):
- Suite: 476 passed, 7 skipped. Before the fix it was 473 + 7, and the difference is the 3 new tests. The 1 warning is pytest_bdd's unknown mark "wip", which comes from the HT-003 skips and is unrelated.
- Coverage: 98.52% total; horizon_playwright.py 96%.
- ruff check src/ tests/ is clean. mypy src/ tests/ is clean over 65 files.
- Clean index (rm beadloom.db, reindex): lint --strict rc 0, sync-check rc 0, doctor rc 0.
- Secrets: the lines added in 6315ccf..HEAD (excluding .beads) contain no credential material. The one new log line carries only the bound in ms.

Sabotage. Each edit was a precise string replace, reversed the same way. The selection was 10 log-off tests in test_horizon_playwright.py (-k log_off), 10 passed at baseline, and the tree was clean after each step.
- S1, drop the wait (plain click): 7 failed, among them test_a_log_off_waits_for_the_brokers_kill_session_answer_before_reloading and ..._never_answered_is_not_confirmed.
- S1b, the pre-fix behaviour (click, then a fixed 1 s wait): 2 failed. test_a_log_off_waits_for_the_brokers_kill_session_answer_before_reloading failed with HorizonClientError logoff_not_confirmed (cut off), and ..._never_answered_ failed on its warning text. The 1.5 s answer proves the wait.
- S2, shorten the bound (FAST.kill_session_answer_ms 3_000 -> 500, below the 1.5 s answer): 2 failed. The slow-answer test failed logoff_not_confirmed, so the shortened bound fails closed. The never-answered test failed on the "3000 ms" text.
- S4, predicate fooled (any /broker/xml response, so the fixture's sibling set-last-user-activity releases the wait): 7 failed, including the slow-answer test. The fixture's decoy works.
- S5, swallow a failed OK click (drop "if not clicked: raise"): 1 failed, test_a_log_off_whose_confirmation_never_shows_fails_without_awaiting_an_answer.
- S3, arm the wait after the click: 10 passed. See the nitpick.

Minor:
1. horizon_playwright.py _answers_kill_session (lines 520-523): the predicate decodes every page response's request body before it checks the path. Request.post_data is a strict UTF-8 .decode(). I probed this in a scratch script, scratchpad/ht-tvn.4/probe_decode.py: a page POST with a non-UTF-8 body during the wait made expect_response raise a Playwright Error "'utf-8' codec can't decode byte 0xff". That error is not PlaywrightTimeoutError. So it escapes the except, _step turns it into LOGOFF_NOT_CONFIRMED at the OK click, and the fresh-list confirmation never runs, even when the kill-session was sent. This fails closed, but any unrelated binary POST in that window (telemetry, uploads) turns it into a false failure. Recommendation: check the URL path first and read the body only for /broker/xml responses, for example "if BROKER_XML_PATH not in urlsplit(response.url).path: return False", then the tag check. A decode guard (post_data_buffer and "in" on bytes) also works.
2. The success path logs nothing. The SPEC lists "how long the broker takes to answer kill-session" as not measured. BRIEF BEAD-03 asks for it from the log ("the kill-session request leaves and gets its answer before the reload (per the journal)"). As it stands, the log can show only that the warning is absent. It cannot show the answer's status or how long it took, and the 30 s bound needs that number to be sized. Also, any status (401/500) counts as "answered". That is safe, because the fresh list decides, but nothing records it. Recommendation: after the with block, log at info "Horizon kill-session answered: <status> after <ms> ms" (event.value.status and the elapsed time). The live check (ht-28a) can then read the answer, its status and its timing from the log.

Nitpick:
- No test pins "armed before the OK click". S3 (click, then arm) passes 10/10, because the fixture's 40 ms hop and 0-1.5 s answers always come after re-arming. The code is correct as written. A regression would cost a 30 s wait and then the fresh-list decision, not a false result. A deterministic pin needs an answer that is guaranteed to arrive before Python regains control, which a localhost fixture cannot promise. If you want one anyway, a 0-hop, 0-delay mode that asserts the warning is absent in the happy path catches it most of the time. Otherwise leave it to code review.

Layering, cohesion and typing: nothing found. The adapter imports only playwright and the domain, and there is one new method with one named responsibility. Response is typed and the new code has no Any or type: ignore. The fixture-only assumptions (set-last-user-activity, the cut-off on logout) are labelled as the fixture's own in the fixture header, the test docstring and the SPEC Testing section.

Independence: review-brief --release withheld the author's account (no verdict recorded yet). I read the 9f243d8 commit body, which carries the author's framing, at the start, along with ht-tvn.2's comments. I did not read ht-tvn.3's comments.

What changed

The bound is HorizonTimeouts.kill_session_answer_ms = 30_000, with the reason in its comment. Past the bound the adapter logs "Horizon kill-session unanswered after N ms" and goes on to the fresh-list poll, which fails closed. The page is still left on a fresh list, so the check-out's second desktop_status still reads the broker. An OK click that fails is re-raised (LOGOFF_NOT_CONFIRMED at once) and is never read as "unanswered".
- Fixture JS: kill-session is a POST of a <broker> XML document to /broker/xml (it was /fixture/kill-session JSON before). OK also sends <set-last-user-activity/> to /broker/xml, answered at once, so the predicate must pick the kill-session's answer. With credential_cleanup on, the page posts <do-logout/> on beforeunload by keepalive fetch (the bundle's _sendLogoutAction, LogoutFromBroker, sendFetch). A behaviour flag logoff_dialog=false leaves the confirmation hidden.
- Fixture server (test module): /broker/xml dispatches kill-session, do-logout and set-last-user-activity. The broker acts on kill-session when it answers, after kill_session_answer_s. A logout of that web session before the answer cuts it off: event "kill-session-cut-off", session kept. kill_session_unanswered holds the request until teardown (released Event, 30 s cap). Logged-out tokens go in a set, so token minting is unchanged.

Coverage TOTAL 99 % (horizon_playwright.py 96 %; the new lines are all covered, and the remaining misses predate this bead). ruff check src tests clean; ruff format --check clean on both touched .py; mypy src tests: 0 issues in 65 files.

Sabotage (one exact replacement each, -k log_off, restored by the reverse replacement and checked against sha256 6979dd4bba24 every time; a final -k log_off run on the restored file was all green)

- S1, drop the wait (plain OK click): 7 failed (through_the_tile_menu, after_reading_the_state, the_portal_never_confirms, only_once_a_fresh_list, through_a_fresh_login, waits_for_the_brokers_kill_session_answer, never_answered). The reload comes before the 40 ms hop, so no kill-session leaves at all.
- S2, bound shortened to 1_000 ms, below the fixture's 1.5 s: 2 failed (waits_for_the_brokers_kill_session_answer_before_reloading, whose_kill_session_is_never_answered_is_not_confirmed).

API CHANGE (application public API for BEAD-07 CLI; deviations from PLAN BEAD-03):

A third module, application/windowed_run.py: WindowedRun(calendar, clock, notifier, window: Window, policy: RetryPolicy), frozen; run(kind: RunKind, attempt: Callable[[], AttemptResult], *, force=False) -> RunReport. AttemptResult(outcome: Outcome, at: datetime, reason: Reason | None = None, screenshot: Path | None = None). Why: the verdict -> decide -> retry -> one-report loop is identical for both use cases (~60 lines); writing it twice would duplicate the rule that holds "exactly one notification per run". Scope deviation: the coordinator named only checkin.py/checkout.py; the new file is inside this bead's own package, which no other wave-2 bead touches.
2. Constructors are not PLAN's MorningCheckin(client, calendar, notifier, clock, artifacts, settings). They are MorningCheckin(client, clock, runner: WindowedRun, desktop: str, hold: timedelta) and EveningCheckout(client, clock, runner: WindowedRun, desktop: str); both .run(*, force=False) -> RunReport. The CLI builds one WindowedRun per kind (checkin window vs checkout window, same calendar/clock/notifier/policy). No Settings: application must not import infrastructure.config, so the CLI unpacks Settings into these values.
3. No ArtifactStore argument: HorizonClient has no screenshot method, the adapter puts the screenshot into HorizonClientError, so the use case had nothing to ask the store. The CLI hands the store to the adapter (as PLAN BEAD-06 already does).
4. application/__init__ re-exports MorningCheckin, EveningCheckout, WindowedRun, AttemptResult.

Contract the use cases rely on from HorizonClient (for BEAD-06 ht-xlh / BEAD-13 probe): (a) desktop_status(name) must work while the desktop is open on #/desktop (RFC: broker XML from the authenticated context; the tile is not on that page); (b) login() is called again after disconnect() closed the browser context, and again on every retry after a failure; (c) checkin calls disconnect() in a finally once open_desktop returned, so it may follow a failed desktop_status.

Mapping decided here: SKIP_NON_WORKING_DAY -> SKIPPED/NON_WORKING_DAY; SKIP_LATE and SKIP_EARLY -> SKIPPED/WINDOW_MISSED (only when no attempt was made); GIVE_UP, or a window that closes between retries, -> FAILED with the LAST failure's reason and screenshot. Unconfirmed check-in -> DESKTOP_DID_NOT_OPEN; unconfirmed log off -> LOGOFF_NOT_CONFIRMED; no session at the first look -> SKIPPED/ALREADY_LOGGED_OFF, not retried. Any exception other than HorizonClientError from an attempt is a failed attempt with Reason.UNEXPECTED (retried); its message is never logged (type + traceback frames only), because adapter text may quote what it typed. Report time: check-in success = the moment open_desktop returned (before the hold); check-out success = the moment the log off was confirmed; skips/failures = when the run ended.

Known gap (domain, not fixed here): Reason has no member for "started before the window", so SKIP_EARLY renders as "the run started after its window", which is false for an early start. Needs a domain Reason (e.g. WINDOW_NOT_OPEN) and its _REASON_TEXT; owner: coordinator.

Scope: the whole HT-001 range, main...bb62fcc (126 files), reviewed against PRD, RFC,

The tree was clean and equal to HEAD.

== Measurements ==
- pytest: 442 collected, 442 passed (421 unit+acceptance, 21 Playwright on the fixture).
  Line coverage is 96.38 % with the floor at 80 %.
- ruff check src/ tests/: clean. mypy --strict: clean on src (20 files) and src+tests (64).
- mutmut over src/horizon_tracker/domain/: 111 mutants, 111 killed, 0 survived, 0 skipped.
- Clean index (rm beadloom.db, reindex): lint --strict exit 0, doctor exit 0,

- beadloom diff --since main: 5 nodes added (horizon-tracker, cli, application, domain,

- PRD scenarios: 12 of 12 are present in tests/acceptance/features, names verbatim.
- Secrets: git grep finds only test fakes. Nothing in .beads/issues.jsonl or the commit
  bodies. .env and artifacts/ are gitignored.

== Sabotage (each reverted by a reverse edit, then diffed against HEAD: identical) ==
| # | Sabotage | Red (named) |
| 1 | domain/session.py imports infrastructure.clock | lint --strict exit 1: architecture-layers + no-dependency-cycles (domain->infrastructure) |
| 2 | telegram._redact returns text unredacted | test_no_log_record_from_any_logger_carries_the_token_or_the_chat_id[network-down], [description-echoes-token] |

- Architecture: PASS. cli -> infrastructure|application -> domain. The ports are declared in

- Security: PASS. The password goes only to #password. Screenshots use an allowlist of

- Doc freshness: PASS. The layer READMEs, cli.md and architecture.md name the current

  after_disconnect), Notifier.send(report), WindowedRun, Probe/DryRun, the env table). The
  feature nodes are BEAD-12's scope.

== Major ==
1. .github/workflows/ci.yml:62 and pyproject.toml:57-60. Severity: Major.
   Issue: the coverage floor is declared but no gate evaluates it. [tool.coverage.report]
   fail_under = 80 takes effect only when pytest runs with --cov. CI runs
   `uv run pytest -q -rs`, addopts has no --cov, and beadloom ci does not run the suite.
   PLAN BEAD-10 asks for "Coverage >= 80 % over src/, a report in CI". Today the floor is met
   (96.4 %) only because someone ran it by hand. The day it drops, nothing goes red. This
   is the class the project layer warns about: a gate that reads as present and checks
   nothing.
   Recommendation: make the CI step `uv run pytest -q -rs --cov --cov-report=term-missing`,
   so that fail_under fails the run. Pin it with a case in
   tests/unit/deploy/test_ci_workflow.py (the pytest step carries --cov). Add Minor 2's
   concurrency setting in the same change, so that the reported figure is true.

== Minor ==
1. tests/integration/infrastructure/test_horizon_playwright.py, in
   test_the_password_never_leaves_the_adapter. Issue: the assertion
   `PASSWORD.encode() not in path.read_bytes()` over the screenshot files cannot fail. A PNG
   holds compressed pixels, never the typed text, and a password field renders as dots
   anyway. Sabotage 6 photographs the login page and this test stays green. The real guard
   is test_a_rejected_login_takes_no_screenshot_of_the_login_page, and it bites.
   Recommendation: replace the byte search with an assertion on which routes the adapter
   asked the artifact store to photograph, as the allowlist test does. Or drop it and let
   the allowlist test carry the claim, so that this test does not report a protection it
   does not measure.
2. pyproject.toml [tool.coverage.run]. Issue: there is no `concurrency`, and Playwright's
   sync API runs on greenlets, so the lines it executes are under-counted. horizon_playwright
   reads 87 % with lines 160-162 and 221-233 "missed". With `concurrency = ["greenlet",
   "thread"]` the same 21 tests measure 94 %, and those lines are covered. Recommendation:
   add the setting.
3. application/probe.py Probe._chrome, infrastructure/horizon_playwright.py probe(), and
   the RFC Risks row "Chrome on the VPS updated and broke Playwright -> probe in the deploy as a
   smoke". Issue: the probe only checks Path.is_file on the binary and reads index.html
   through Playwright's request context. It never launches Chrome, so the deploy smoke
   cannot catch the risk the RFC assigns to it. Separately, the port docstring and the PRD
   scenario say "portal version", but the adapter returns bundle file names
   (app-htmlaccess.<hash>.js), and the BDD scenario passes on the fake's "fake-2312".
   Recommendation: have the probe launch headless Chrome at chrome_path, read
   browser.version and close it, with no navigation. Alternatively, correct the RFC
   mitigation. Then either read a real version or rename the contract to "client bundles".
4. application/probe.py DryRun.plan, _checkin_steps and _checkout_steps. Issue: DryRun
   re-implements WindowedRun's first decision (forced RUN with source None, otherwise
   resolve + decide), and it hand-writes the steps that MorningCheckin and EveningCheckout
   perform. These are two copies that can drift silently: the dry run would then describe a
   run that no longer exists. Recommendation: expose WindowedRun's first decision as a
   method that DryRun calls, and keep each use case's step list beside the use case.
   _FIRST_ATTEMPT is also defined three times (schedule, probe, windowed_run).
5. cli.py:186 (`adapters.artifacts.prune()`) and the adapter teardown in open_adapters.
   Issue: the "one report per run" invariant holds only inside WindowedRun. An OSError from
   prune aborts the run before any attempt, sends no Telegram message, and prints a
   traceback. A PlaywrightError from browser.close() after a SUCCEEDED report exits 1, so
   systemd marks a successful run failed. Recommendation: make prune best-effort (catch
   OSError and log the type), and make close() log and swallow a PlaywrightError.
6. application/windowed_run.py and domain/schedule.py, against the PRD goal "a tolerance of at
   most 5 minutes". Issue: the window bounds when an attempt STARTS, not when the logon
   happens. A retry started at 07:59:50 can open the desktop at about 08:01:30 (login 30 s
   plus open 90 s). Recommendation: either document that the window bounds the start
   (CONTEXT row), or end the retry window early by the worst-case attempt duration.
7. application/checkin.py:41. This is a hypothesis to measure in BEAD-13, not a proven
   defect. The 120 s hold is Clock.sleep, which is time.sleep, and it does not pump
   Playwright's sync event loop. Playwright's guidance is page.wait_for_timeout for that
   reason. Recommendation: on the first VPS run, confirm that the Blast WebSocket is still
   reported open after the hold. If it is not, let the adapter hold the page (for example
   with a HorizonClient.hold(seconds)).

== Nitpick ==
- ConfigError and HorizonClientError have no common project base exception.
- morning_checkin.feature "reports success with the recorded time": the Given "held open
  for 120 seconds" has no observable consequence in its Thens.

Not closed: a Major requires a fix cycle (review role protocol).

comments.text:
API CHANGE (public interface = the horizon CLI + the environment; for the deploy bead ht-2h2, the workflows bead ht-spa and the docs bead ht-6rw). Commit f0f958c.

COMMANDS
- horizon --version            -> "horizon, version 0.1.0", exit 0
- horizon --help               -> lists exactly: checkin, checkout, probe
- horizon checkin  [--dry-run] [--force]
- horizon checkout [--dry-run] [--force]
- horizon probe
--force   : ignore the window and the calendar (manual run from the VPS); the report then says the calendar was not asked.
--dry-run : print the plan to stdout and exit 0; never calls login or any other Horizon method, sends no Telegram report, prunes nothing. The calendar IS asked (read-only GET to isdayoff.ru) unless --force is also given. Both flags combine.

EXIT CODES
- checkin/checkout: 1 iff the run's report is Outcome.FAILED; 0 for SUCCEEDED and for every deliberate skip (non-working day, before/after the window, already logged off). systemd marks the unit failed exactly on a failed run.
- checkin/checkout --dry-run: 0.
- probe: 1 if any check FAILED (portal unreachable / no bundles, Chrome binary missing); 0 otherwise. An unreachable isdayoff.ru is DEGRADED (runs fall back to Mon-Fri) and does NOT fail the probe -> a deploy smoke `horizon probe` is not broken by an isdayoff outage.
- every command: 1 on a configuration error, logged on stderr as "configuration error: <VAR>: <problem>" (no traceback, no value of a credential). A Telegram token that TelegramNotifier refuses (e.g. a trailing newline from .env) is reported as "configuration error: TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN: ..." before anything runs; nothing is stripped silently.

OUTPUT
- stdout: only the dry-run plan and the probe lines. Probe lines, in order: "settings: ok - portal <HORIZON_URL>, desktop '<HORIZON_DESKTOP>', check-in HH:MM-HH:MM, check-out HH:MM-HH:MM, <tz>", "portal: ok|failed - <HTML Access bundles: ...|no answer: <reason>>", "calendar: ok|degraded - ...", "chrome: ok|failed - found at|not found at <HT_CHROME_PATH>".
- stderr: logging, level INFO, format "%(asctime)s %(levelname)s %(name)s: %(message)s", handler on the "horizon_tracker" package logger (not root). The journal of a systemd unit captures it; there is no log file (PLAN said "stderr and file": the file is left to journald, so no rotation code).

ENVIRONMENT READ (Settings.from_env(os.environ), unchanged from ht-c5q)
Required: HORIZON_URL, HORIZON_USERNAME, HORIZON_PASSWORD, TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN, TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID.
Optional (default): HORIZON_DESKTOP ("DEV desktop"), HT_TIMEZONE (Europe/Moscow), HT_CHECKIN_WINDOW (07:55-08:00), HT_CHECKOUT_WINDOW (17:00-17:05), HT_HOLD_SECONDS (120), HT_CHROME_PATH (/usr/bin/google-chrome), HT_ARTIFACTS_DIR (/opt/horizon-tracker/artifacts).
